title: Ethiopian Smoked Fish
community: Lake communities — the traditional preserved lake fish
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Smoked Lake Fish — whole fish salted, spiced with berbere and garlic, and slowly smoked over fragrant wood until deeply flavoured and preserved. The traditional lake community preservation technique — smoked fish is used in stews, eaten as-is, and carried on long journeys.
longDesc: Smoked fish is the preservation technique of Ethiopia's lake communities — when the catch is larger than can be eaten fresh, the fish is salted, spiced, and smoked. The smoking adds flavour complexity and extends the shelf life dramatically. Smoked fish is used in stews and eaten as a snack.
ingredients: 1 kg whole fish — tilapia or catfish
// Wood for smoking: olive wood, acacia, or fruit wood
equipment: Smoker or covered grill with indirect heat
steps: Rub salt, berbere, and garlic over all surfaces and into score marks.
Prepare smoker at 70—80°C (low temperature, cold smoke).
Smoke fish for 6—8 hours, refuelling as needed.
The fish is ready when deeply golden, firm, and fragrant.
chefTips: Low temperature — this is preservation smoking, not cooking smoking.
The berbere adds complexity to the smoke flavour.
Smoked fish keeps 2 weeks at room temperature in a dry place.
commonMistakes: Too high temperature — cooks rather than smokes.
cookingScience: Cold smoking at 70—80°C produces volatile phenol compounds from the wood combustion — these phenols deposit on the fish surface and have antimicrobial properties, inhibiting bacterial and fungal growth. Combined with the salt's desiccating effect, they extend shelf life dramatically.
sustainabilityTips: The most sustainable fish preservation — uses local wood and produces zero packaging waste.
storage: Wrapped in cloth 2 weeks at room temperature. Refrigerate 1 month.
reheating: Use in stews or eat as-is.
culturalNote: Smoked lake fish is the food preservation wisdom of Ethiopia's lake communities — developed over centuries of observation to make the most of abundant fishing seasons and provide protein through lean periods.
